cleanIntro:
This guide follows Savage's Impulse rifle manual; check your variant against it. The book covers the Impulse family of straight-pull rifles and never names the Mountain Hunter.

Savage's own cleaning procedure takes out only the bolt assembly: unload, press the bolt release, draw the bolt out, and clean the bore from the chamber end. Savage also publishes taking the bolt head off the bolt and lifting the stock off the action, with the action-screw torque for putting it back; those are in DEEP CLEAN.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, Safety Selector to the rear (Full Safe)
steps.action: This guide follows Savage's Impulse rifle manual; check your variant against it. Point the muzzle in a safe direction and keep it there. The Safety Selector is at the rear of the receiver tang: slide it rearward until the Red Indicator is hidden. That is Full Safe. Red showing means Ready to Fire.
steps.prose: The safety blocks the trigger, not the bolt: on the Impulse the bolt still opens and closes with the safety on, and the selector never moves back to safe on its own when the bolt is worked.
steps.quote: Sliding the Safety Selector rearward, the Red Indicator is hidden from view and the safety is on
steps.cite: Savage Arms Impulse Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 1.1 Two Position Safety, printed p.3 (PDF p.5)

steps.title: Magazine out, release forward or rearward by model
steps.action: Press the Magazine Release and take the magazine out of the rifle. Savage prints two magazine styles, a Savage style and an AICS style, and the release moves forward on one and rearward on the other depending on model. Use the way your rifle's release actually moves.
steps.prose: The book does not say which magazine this variant carries. Look at the rifle, not this guide.
steps.quote: Press the Magazine Release either forward or rearward depending on model
steps.cite: Savage Arms Impulse Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3.3 Unloading Procedure, printed p.11 (PDF p.13)

steps.title: Bolt back, round out of the chamber
steps.action: Keep fingers away from the trigger. If the rifle has been fired, simply pull the Bolt Handle rearward to take out the fired case. If it has not been fired, the bolt is locked: press the top of the Quick Release Button at the rear of the bolt forward with your thumb, then pull the Bolt Handle rearward to take out the unfired round.
steps.prose: A straight-pull bolt that has not been fired will not come back on a plain pull. That resistance is the lock, not a jam; the Quick Release Button is the way past it.
steps.quote: If the firearm has not been fired, press forward on the top of the Quick Release Button with your thumb and pull rearward on the Bolt Handle
steps.cite: Savage Arms Impulse Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3.3 Unloading Procedure, printed p.11 (PDF p.13)

steps.title: LOOK into the chamber, and feel it
steps.action: With the bolt back, look into the chamber and check it with a finger as well, then check it a second time. The magazine out and a round ejected do not prove the chamber is empty.
steps.prose: Savage asks for both checks, seen and felt, and asks for them twice. If the extractor slips, the round can stay in the chamber while the bolt comes back.
steps.quote: Visibly and physically inspect the chamber to be clear of ammunition. Double check the chamber to ensure it is completely free of ammunition.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Impulse Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 3.3 Unloading Procedure, printed p.11 (PDF p.13)
steps.warn: In a situation where the extractor fails, the bolt may not extract the cartridge.

steps.title: Bolt release forward and in
steps.action: With the bolt assembly at the rear of its travel, it stops against the bolt release on the receiver. Let go of the bolt. Slide the Bolt Release forward and press it into the receiver.
steps.prose: Take your hand off the bolt first, as Savage says; the release is worked on its own.
steps.quote: Without holding the Bolt Assembly, slide the Bolt Release forward and depress it into the receiver
steps.cite: Savage Arms Impulse Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 2.4 Bolt Assembly Removal, printed p.6 (PDF p.8)

steps.title: Bolt assembly out of the receiver
steps.action: Keep the Bolt Release held in and draw the bolt assembly straight back out of the receiver.
steps.prose: If the bolt stops, the release has come back out. Press it in again and keep holding it.
steps.quote: While holding the Bolt Release in, pull the Bolt Assembly out of the receiver.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Impulse Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 2.4 Bolt Assembly Removal, printed p.6 (PDF p.8)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the rifle and the bolt assembly. That is all Savage's cleaning procedure takes apart: unload, take the bolt assembly out, and clean. Taking the bolt head off the bolt and the stock off the action are published separately and are in DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: For routine cleaning, stop here. The bolt assembly stays whole.
steps.quote: Remove the Bolt Assembly as described in section 2.4.
steps.cite: Savage Arms Impulse Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 7.2 Cleaning and Care of Your Firearm, printed p.17 (PDF p.19)

deepSteps.title: Uncock the bolt: press the Extraction Plunger
deepSteps.action: With the bolt assembly out of the rifle, rotate the Bolt Handle slightly rearward to take pressure off, then press the spring-loaded Extraction Plunger on top of the bolt assembly with your thumb or a non-marring object, and let the Bolt Handle rotate slowly forward. The bolt assembly is now uncocked.
deepSteps.prose: Let the handle come forward under control; it is spring-loaded.
deepSteps.quote: depress the spring-loaded Extraction Plunger at the top of the bolt assembly with your thumb or any non-marring object
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms Impulse Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 2.7 Bolt Head Removal and Installation, printed p.9 (PDF p.10)

deepSteps.title: Bolt head off: press the lock plunger, turn, pull
deepSteps.action: Press the rear of the Bolt Head Lock Plunger with your finger. The bolt head can then be rotated counter-clockwise and pulled away from the bolt assembly.
deepSteps.prose: Note how the slots line up as it comes off: going back, the slot in the bolt head lines up with the large slot in the bolt body first, then with the small slot once it is turned home.
deepSteps.quote: Depress the rear of the Bolt Head Lock Plunger with your finger
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms Impulse Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 2.7 Bolt Head Removal and Installation, printed p.9 (PDF p.10)

deepSteps.title: Stock off: front action screw
deepSteps.action: Bolt out, magazine out, rifle confirmed empty. Support the rifle upside down with the muzzle away from you in a safe direction. Find the two action screws; with flush-fit magazines both are visible, one in front of the magazine well and one at the rear, and with AICS-style magazines the rear one is reached through the access point in the magazine latch. With a 1/8 in hex key, loosen and remove the front action screw.
deepSteps.prose: The two screws are different lengths: the longer one belongs at the rear. Keep them apart.
deepSteps.quote: loosen and remove the Front Action Screw securing the stock to the receiver
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms Impulse Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 5.1 Stock Removal, printed p.14 (PDF p.16)

deepSteps.title: Rear action screw, then lift the stock
deepSteps.action: With the same 1/8 in hex key, remove the rear action screw. Then lift the stock straight up off the action.
deepSteps.prose: Lift straight; the trigger group sits down into the trigger guard area of the stock.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the Stock by lifting it straight up.
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms Impulse Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 5.1 Stock Removal, printed p.14 (PDF p.16)

deepSteps.title: Look over the AccuTrigger, and this is where Savage stops
deepSteps.action: With the stock off, look over the AccuTrigger and its adjustment spring for damage and for debris such as twigs or grass. Savage's book takes the rifle no further apart. Anything deeper in the mechanism goes to a qualified gunsmith or the Savage Arms Service Department.
deepSteps.prose: Inspect only. Nothing in the trigger comes apart here.
deepSteps.quote: With the stock removed, carefully inspect the AccuTrigger and adjustment spring for damage or foreign debris
deepSteps.cite: Savage Arms Impulse Instruction Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Section 7.1 Routine Maintenance, printed p.16 (PDF p.18)
deepSteps.warn: In depth mechanical issues or questions as well as periodic examinations should be referred to a qualified gunsmith or Savage Arms Service Department.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Lay the rifle level with the ejection port facing down on a soft surface.
Put a little powder solvent on the brush and run the rod through the bore several times, always starting from the chamber end and out the muzzle.
Change to a patch tip and push clean patches through from the chamber end several times.
Push one patch wet with gun oil through the bore, then a dry patch to take the excess off.
⚠ Look through the bore and make sure no piece of patch or other obstruction is left before the bolt goes back in.

cleaning.name: BOLT ASSEMBLY
tasks: While the bolt is out, look over the bolt head, extractor and ejector for damage or excessive wear.
Put a light coat of oil on the whole bolt body, including the large groove for the bolt release.
Put a small drop of oil on top of the Extraction Plunger and let it coat the plunger.
Put a drop or two of oil on the Striker Assembly at the rear of the underside of the bolt assembly.

cleaning.name: RECEIVER AND OUTSIDE
tasks: Lightly oil the whole bolt raceway in the receiver.
Wipe off mud, twigs and grass with a soft cloth.
Put a thin coat of gun oil on every cleaned metal surface, rubbing where needed to remove any sign of rust.
Run your fingers gently down the outside of the barrel, feeling for bulges or damage, and check the scope rings and the sling studs.

reassembly: If the stock is off: lower it onto the action with the trigger group seating into the trigger guard area, fit the trigger guard/magazine well into the stock, and start the action screws a few turns only: the longer screw at the rear, the shorter at the front.
Stand the rifle on its recoil pad with the barrel up, press down on the barrel to seat the recoil lug in the stock, and tighten the rear action screw first, then the front, to 55 in-lbs.

If the bolt head is off: fit it with its slot lined up with the large slot in the bolt body, push it home, turn it clockwise until its slot lines up with the small slot in the bolt body, and press the front of the Bolt Head Lock Plunger flush.

Cock the bolt assembly: hold the bolt body and rotate the Bolt Handle rearward as far as it goes until the Extraction Plunger is fully visible and the handle locks back. The bolt only goes in cocked, with the bolt head lined up.
Safety to Full Safe, magazine out, and look through the receiver into the barrel to be sure it is clear.

Line the large slot on the left of the bolt assembly up with the left side of the receiver and the Bolt Release, rotate the whole bolt slightly clockwise, and slide it in until you meet slight resistance; then rotate it slightly counter-clockwise and keep sliding until the Bolt Release snaps into its slot.
Push the Bolt Handle forward to close the bolt; when it is properly closed the handle rotates forward slightly.
fncheck: With the rifle confirmed unloaded and the muzzle in a safe direction, check the Two Position Safety as Savage asks after every cleaning: slide the Safety Selector forward and the Red Indicator shows (Ready to Fire), slide it rearward and the red is hidden (Full Safe). Leave it on Full Safe. Work the bolt: it should close with the handle rotating forward slightly at the end. After the stock has been off, make sure the action screws are tight. If anything feels or sounds different, stop and have a qualified gunsmith or the Savage Arms Service Department look at it.
